children: Company Held Several Meetings with Corporate Security Leaders, Government Officials and Partners Over 2.5 Days in Atlanta; Over 50 New Enterprise and Government Opportunities of more than 10,000 Employees Each Entering Pipeline
Bond Co-Sponsored the Women in Security and NextGen Awards with Amazon

, the creator of the world’s first AI-powered Preventative Personal Security platform adopted by leading multinational companies, today reported strong engagement during its recent participation in Global Security Exchange (GSX) 2026, held September 14–16 in Atlanta. GSX, organized by ASIS International, is one of the world’s premier gatherings of security professionals, corporate security leaders and innovators.

GSX represented Bond’s first major awareness and lead generation marketing campaign in the past 5 years, as well as the first major security industry exhibition following the expansion of its growth initiatives and listing on Nasdaq in February 2026. It represents a shift from narrowly-focused marketing efforts oriented towards early adopters to casting a much wider market awareness net targeting the early majority of the market. During the multi-day event, Bond’s booth received visitors from over 1,000 corporations and government agencies, many of whom expressed interest in Bond for their employees or customers, including Amazon, Bank of America, Google, Airbnb, ADP, the US Postal Service, and more. Bond’s exhibit included an approximately 1,500-square-foot booth featuring a theater in which the Company delivered live demonstrations of its AI-powered Preventative Personal Security platform, giving security leaders a firsthand look at how Bond extends personal security beyond traditional alert-based solutions by addressing situations before they escalate into emergencies.

Bond’s exhibit focused on expressing the service’s great unique value including the Preventative Personal Security attributes of the solution that have enabled Bond to be certified as a sole supplier by numerous government agencies, as well as the EY ROI report about Bond that concludes Bond actually saves between $180 and $280 per employee per year for corporations who deploy the service by reducing both the number and severity of security incidents, which in turn reduces both the associated direct and indirect costs of those incidents, including but not limited to medical and insurance costs, lost days of work, costs related to employee churn, such as hiring and training replacements, and legal and reputational costs.

“GSX provided an important opportunity to demonstrate Bond’s platform directly to many of the decision-makers responsible for protecting large employee and public populations,” said Doron Kempel, Founder and CEO of Bond. “More than a thousand security professionals came to our booth. Inflection points in the adoption of a new category begin exactly this way. You cast a wide net, you meet a large number of decision-makers in a short period of time, you show them independent economic validation like our EY research, and a meaningful share of those conversations move forward.”

“Our increased investment in growth is designed to not just increase the top of the funnel, but also to change three things at once: the share of meetings that convert to customers, the length of the sales cycle, and the size of each deal. GSX gave us evidence on all three in a single week,” Kempel continued. “More than 50 organizations of 10,000 people or more expressed interest in Bond at this one conference alone. Revolutions require new technologies and new operating models, but they also require leaders who are willing to be early adopters, and we met many of them in Atlanta. We expect the opportunities generated at GSX to convert over the next 6 to 12 months in line with our enterprise and government sales cycles, and we intend to continue investing in the activities that put Bond in front of the people who make these decisions.”
The Company also co-sponsored, alongside Amazon, the Women in Security and NextGen Awards, recognizing established and emerging leaders who are helping shape the future of the security profession.

Bond is an international company headquartered in New York City — with command centers around the world — that is redefining personal security through its AI-powered Preventative Personal Security platform. The company has invested more than $100 million to date in its technology, operations, and global expansion.

Bond offers personal security to more people than any other company globally. Bond is trusted by leading corporations, cities, and universities, and has already supported more than 1.25 million security service requests, including over 10,000 emergencies and life-saving interventions. Bond operates in 28 countries and growing, positioning itself as a new global standard for personal security and peace of mind. Additional information about the Company is available at: www.ourbond.com.
